title: Product Requirement Prompt
description: The single source of truth for PRP structure. hooks/validate-prp-frontmatter.sh is a thin caller of scripts/check-schema.py against this file. The validated object is built by check-schema.py: `frontmatter` is the parsed line-1 YAML block, `sections` maps each `## ` heading text to its ordinal.

frontmatter.description: Line-1 YAML frontmatter. Open to extra fields — see the same note in adr.schema.json.

id.description: Document ID (PRP-NNN). Assigned by /blueprint:sync-ids when missing.

status.description: Lifecycle state, lowercase (unlike ADR/PRD). `complete` is canonical and matches the feature-tracker vocabulary; `completed` is the pre-reconciliation spelling, accepted so downstream PRPs keep validating, and warned about below.

reviewed.description: YYYY-MM-DD the PRP was last refreshed against the codebase.

confidence.description: Readiness score 1-10, written either as an integer or as `N/10`. See skills/confidence-scoring.

then.title: `status: completed` is the pre-reconciliation spelling — use `complete`, which matches feature-tracker.schema.json's canonical vocabulary.

sections.description: Map of `## ` heading text to its 0-based ordinal. Missing sections WARN rather than block, so a PRP can be drafted top-down and saved mid-write. hooks/check-prp-readiness.sh is the gate: it blocks Skill(prp-execute) on the same sections, which is where completeness actually matters. See .claude/rules/hook-block-vs-nudge.md.
sections.title: required `## ` section missing — the ADR/PRP template declares it; add it or run the matching validate skill
